lines.text: Take a triangle. Copy it. Slide the copy a little to the right.
lines.caption: Take a triangle. Copy it. Slide the copy a little to the right.

lines.text: How much of the copied triangle sticks out? Lots of kids answer twenty-four here.
lines.caption: How much of the copied triangle sticks out? Lots of kids answer twenty-four here.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out what's really going on.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out what's really going on.

lines.text: Here's the question. A right triangle has legs twelve and nine.
lines.caption: Here's the question. A right triangle has legs twelve and nine.

lines.text: The triangle is copied, and the copy is slid four to the right, as shown.
lines.caption: The triangle is copied, and the copy is slid four to the right, as shown.

lines.text: What is the area of the shaded part of the copy, the part that does not overlap the original?
lines.caption: What is the area of the shaded part of the copy, the part that does not overlap the original?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know?
lines.caption: So what do we know?

lines.text: The bottom leg is twelve, and the left leg is nine. The square corner is at the bottom left.
lines.caption: The bottom leg is twelve, and the left leg is nine. The square corner is at the bottom left.

lines.text: The copy slides four to the right, along the bottom line.
lines.caption: The copy slides four to the right, along the bottom line.

lines.text: We want the shaded part: the copy, minus the piece both triangles share.
lines.caption: We want the shaded part: the copy, minus the piece both triangles share.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our strategy: find the whole copy, then take away the overlap.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our strategy: find the whole copy, then take away the overlap.

lines.text: The copy is the same triangle. To get its area, we take one over two, times twelve, times nine.
lines.caption: The copy is the same triangle. To get its area, we take one over two, times twelve, times nine.

lines.text: That's fifty-four. So the whole copy is fifty-four.
lines.caption: That's fifty-four. So the whole copy is fifty-four.

lines.text: Now look at the overlap. It's a triangle too!
lines.caption: Now look at the overlap. It's a triangle too!

lines.text: Its square corner is where the copy's left side stands, four along the bottom.
lines.caption: Its square corner is where the copy's left side stands, four along the bottom.

lines.text: Its bottom runs from there to the end of the original. That's twelve minus four, which is eight.
lines.caption: Its bottom runs from there to the end of the original. That's twelve minus four, which is eight.

lines.text: Its slanted side lies along the original's long side. So it has the same slant.
lines.caption: Its slanted side lies along the original's long side. So it has the same slant.

lines.text: A square corner and the same slant mean the same angles. It's a smaller copy of the original.
lines.caption: A square corner and the same slant mean the same angles. It's a smaller copy of the original.

lines.text: Same shape, smaller size. Eight out of twelve is two over three.
lines.caption: Same shape, smaller size. Eight out of twelve is two over three.

lines.text: So its height is two over three of nine. That's six.
lines.caption: So its height is two over three of nine. That's six.

lines.text: The overlap's area is one over two, times eight, times six. That's twenty-four.
lines.caption: The overlap's area is one over two, times eight, times six. That's twenty-four.

lines.text: Now take it away. Fifty-four minus twenty-four is thirty.
lines.caption: Now take it away. Fifty-four minus twenty-four is thirty.

lines.text: The shaded part is thirty! The answer is E.
lines.caption: The shaded part is thirty! The answer is E.

lines.text: Let's try another way. Look at the original triangle this time.
lines.caption: Let's try another way. Look at the original triangle this time.

lines.text: It loses the same overlap. And it has the same area, fifty-four.
lines.caption: It loses the same overlap. And it has the same area, fifty-four.

lines.text: So the part of the original left over is the SAME size as the shaded part!
lines.caption: So the part of the original left over is the SAME size as the shaded part!

lines.text: That remaining part is the strip on the left, four wide.
lines.caption: That remaining part is the strip on the left, four wide.

lines.text: Its left side is nine tall. How tall is its right side?
lines.caption: Its left side is nine tall. How tall is its right side?

lines.text: The long side drops nine as it goes twelve across. That's three for every four.
lines.caption: The long side drops nine as it goes twelve across. That's three for every four.

lines.text: So after four across, it has dropped three. Nine minus three is six.
lines.caption: So after four across, it has dropped three. Nine minus three is six.

lines.text: The strip is a trapezoid, with parallel sides nine and six, and width four.
lines.caption: The strip is a trapezoid, with parallel sides nine and six, and width four.

lines.text: A trapezoid's area is the average of its two parallel sides, times the width.
lines.caption: A trapezoid's area is the average of its two parallel sides, times the width.

lines.text: Nine plus six is fifteen. Half is seven and a half. Times four is thirty!
lines.caption: Nine plus six is fifteen. Half is seven and a half. Times four is thirty!

lines.text: Same answer! When would you pick this way? When the strip is easier to see than the overlap.
lines.caption: Same answer! When would you pick this way? When the strip is easier to see than the overlap.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Twenty-four is the overlap. It answers the wrong question. We wanted the part outside it.
lines.caption: Twenty-four is the overlap. It answers the wrong question. We wanted the part outside it.

lines.text: Twenty-seven is half of fifty-four. But nothing in the picture cuts the copy in half.
lines.caption: Twenty-seven is half of fifty-four. But nothing in the picture cuts the copy in half.

lines.text: Eighteen is what you'd get if you called the strip a triangle, base four, height nine.
lines.caption: Eighteen is what you'd get if you called the strip a triangle, base four, height nine.

lines.text: But the strip's right side is six tall. A triangle would come to a point there.
lines.caption: But the strip's right side is six tall. A triangle would come to a point there.

lines.text: Twenty-eight is what you'd get if the long side dropped four, not three, for every four across.
lines.caption: Twenty-eight is what you'd get if the long side dropped four, not three, for every four across.

lines.text: Then the right side would be five, and the trapezoid would give twenty-eight.
lines.caption: Then the right side would be five, and the trapezoid would give twenty-eight.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Ask what the shaded part is, then check every height.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Ask what the shaded part is, then check every height.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new triangle.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new triangle.

lines.text: Its bottom leg is ten, and its left leg is five.
lines.caption: Its bottom leg is ten, and its left leg is five.

lines.text: The copy slides four to the right. What is the area of the shaded part?
lines.caption: The copy slides four to the right. What is the area of the shaded part?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The whole triangle's area is one over two, times ten, times five. That's twenty-five.
lines.caption: Let's check. The whole triangle's area is one over two, times ten, times five. That's twenty-five.

lines.text: The overlap's bottom is ten minus four, which is six. Six out of ten is three over five.
lines.caption: The overlap's bottom is ten minus four, which is six. Six out of ten is three over five.

lines.text: Its height is three over five of five. That's three.
lines.caption: Its height is three over five of five. That's three.

lines.text: The overlap is one over two, times six, times three. That's nine.
lines.caption: The overlap is one over two, times six, times three. That's nine.

lines.text: Twenty-five minus nine is sixteen!
lines.caption: Twenty-five minus nine is sixteen!

lines.text: Check with the strip. Its sides are five and three, and it's four wide.
lines.caption: Check with the strip. Its sides are five and three, and it's four wide.

lines.text: Five plus three is eight. Half is four. Four times four is sixteen. It matches!
lines.caption: Five plus three is eight. Half is four. Four times four is sixteen. It matches!

lines.text: If you found sixteen, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found sixteen, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Slide a triangle along its base, and the overlap is a smaller copy of the same shape.
lines.caption: Slide a triangle along its base, and the overlap is a smaller copy of the same shape.

lines.text: Find the whole, take away the overlap, and you have the part left over.
lines.caption: Find the whole, take away the overlap, and you have the part left over.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
